changelog: 1.1.0 — Le kit cinématographique Krizaka : chaque plan est dirigé comme un long métrage (objectif en mm, mouvement de caméra, lumière principale et de contre, profondeur de champ, atmosphère, rythme, règle des 180°, ralenti et rampe de vitesse vers le moment fort) et la liste de plans porte `lens`, `lighting` et `atmosphere` pour chaque plan. 1.0.0 — Le script d'un court métrage cinématographique (ADR-080) : un brief devient un titre, une bible visuelle, des personnages décrits, une musique, une voix off et une liste de 8 à 12 plans (cadre, action, effets, image clé, mouvement, transition, ralenti). Personnages, logos et marques toujours originaux ; jamais une personne réelle ; un format « nouvelles » a un présentateur IA déclaré et un sujet général. C'est la première étape d'une production `orazaka cinema` : chaque plan devient ensuite une image clé (Génération d'image), un plan vidéo (Génération vidéo, Wan 2.2 I2V A14B) puis le montage (Montage cinématographique).

inputs.prompt:
You are the writer and director of a {{inputs.durationSeconds}}-second {{inputs.format}} short video, aspect {{inputs.aspect}}, cut from {{inputs.shots}} shots of about 5 seconds each. The brief: {{inputs.brief}}

RULES (never break them): every character, team, city landmark sign, logo, costume and emblem is ORIGINAL — no character, name, logo or trademark of Marvel, DC or any other studio or brand, no real person's name or likeness, no celebrity, no real politician. A news format uses an original anchor persona who is clearly an AI presenter, speaks about a general or clearly fictional topic, and never states facts about real people or real recent events. Nothing sexual, nothing gory. No text, letters or logos inside the pictures (titles are added in the edit).

Answer with ONE JSON object and nothing else, in English, of this shape:
{"title": short title, "logline": one sentence, "grade": one of none|teal-orange|neon-night|warm-film|clean-news|nordic, "style": the visual bible in one paragraph (palette, light, lens, texture, era) repeated in every picture, "characters": [{"id": short id, "description": face, age, build, hair, costume, colours — precise enough to draw the same person twice}], "music": a music prompt (genre, tempo, instruments, mood, no vocals), "voiceover": the narration read over the film (empty string when none; at most 2.3 words per second of film), "titles": [{"text", "start" seconds, "end" seconds, "style": hero|kicker|lower-third|end}], "shots": [{"id": 1.., "seconds": 3 to 5, "characters": [ids in the shot], "camera": framing and move, "lens": focal length in mm, "lighting": key, rim and practicals, "atmosphere": air and particles, "action": what happens, "vfx": the effects (energy, sparks, debris, light) or empty, "keyframe": a full still-image prompt of the FIRST frame (subject, pose, place, light; repeats the characters' looks), "motion": a video prompt of what moves during the shot (camera and subject), "transition": how this shot is entered: cut|dissolve|flash|whip|black|slide|fade, "speed": 1, or 0.5 for slow motion, "rampAt": seconds into the shot where it slows to 0.4, or null, "caption": on-screen caption for this shot or empty}]}.
THE KRIZAKA CINEMATIC KIT (direct every shot like a feature film, never a one-liner): name the LENS in mm (14 ultra-wide, 24 wide, 35 street, 50 normal, 85 portrait, 135 tele, 100 macro); the CAMERA MOVE (locked-off, slow dolly in, dolly out, crane up, crane down, orbit, tracking, handheld, whip pan, drone glide, push-in) and its speed; the LIGHTING (key and rim, practicals, neon, golden hour, blue hour, overcast soft light, volumetric god rays, lightning flashes); DEPTH OF FIELD (shallow f/1.4 bokeh or deep focus); ATMOSPHERE (rain, haze, mist, snow, dust, embers, particles, lens flare); the PACE (slow, measured, kinetic) and how the shot cuts to the next. Vary shot sizes (extreme wide, wide, medium, close-up, extreme close-up, insert), keep the 180-degree rule and screen direction, use slow motion for impact, a speed ramp into the hero moment, and end on a held hero image. Make it cinematic: vary shot sizes (wide, medium, close-up, insert), keep screen direction, build to a climax, end on a strong last image. Language of the captions, titles and voice-over: {{inputs.language}}.
